lesson_title: Paper 1 Practice Run: Every Mark Accounted For
hook_text: Borrow R900 000. Repay R2 156 500. The exam question hiding a life lesson about interest.
clip_script: A loan of nine hundred thousand rand is repaid over two hundred and forty equal monthly payments at ten comma five percent per annum compounded monthly. The formula off the information sheet: P equals x times, one minus one plus i to the minus n, over i. The monthly rate: nought comma zero zero eight seven five. The payment lands at eight thousand nine hundred and eighty-five rand and forty-two cents. Now multiply by two hundred and forty: about two comma one six million rand — more than double the amount borrowed. That comparison sentence is a favourite final subquestion, and the interest alone is one comma two six million.
visual_style: A house-shaped stack of banknotes on one side of a balance scale; each monthly payment slides across as a note until the repaid pile towers to more than double the house, the interest portion glowing a different colour.
mood: Jaw-drop consumer maths — the exam question that doubles as financial literacy.
pacing: Calm formula setup, rhythmic payment ticker accelerating, hard stop on the 2,16 million reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and walk Paper 1 with every mark accounted for.
